title: What Not to Share with AI

cards.prompt:
A chat with an AI app can feel private, but it isn't a diary. Depending on the app, your chats may be **saved**, **read by staff** checking for problems, or **used to train** future models.

So: don't type anything you wouldn't want someone else to read. And your friends' photos and secrets aren't yours to share.

Is each one **fine to type**, or one to **keep private**?
cards.hint: Ask: would it matter if someone else read it later? And is it yours to share?
cards.nudge: Some come with a good-sounding reason, like keeping it safe or getting advice. Does the reason make it safe to type?
cards.explanation: Recipes, made-up ideas and general questions are **fine**. Your name and school, passwords (even "to keep safe"), friends' photos and friends' secrets stay **private**: the chat may be stored, and some of it isn't yours to share.

cards.prompt: You want AI help writing a thank-you letter to your grandma. The letter includes your home address. What's the **safest** way?

options.text: Type it all in: the chatbot forgets after the chat ends
options.nudge: Forgetting in the chat isn't the same as the app deleting it. Your chat may be stored. What could you leave out?

options.text: Use a nickname instead of your name, but keep the address
options.nudge: The address is the private part. How could you get help without it?

options.text: Ask for help with the wording, and leave the address out
Ask the chatbot to promise to keep your address secret
options.nudge: A chatbot can't make that promise: where your chat goes depends on the app. What's safer?

cards.hint: The chatbot only needs to help with the words. Which part does it not need at all?
cards.explanation: The chatbot only needs the **wording**, so leave the address out and add it yourself afterwards. A new chat starting fresh doesn't delete the saved copy of the old one, and a chatbot can't promise anything about where your data goes.

cards.prompt:
Apps ask for [[permissions|app-permission]] to use things like your contacts, location, camera, microphone or photos. You choose what to allow.

You install an AI app that turns a photo of a recipe into a shopping list. As it opens, it asks to see your **contacts** and your **location**.

choices.text: Allow everything, or the app might not work
choices.consequence: A shopping-list app doesn't need your contacts or where you are. Allowing them gives away private things for nothing.

choices.text: Say no to both, and see if the app still works
choices.consequence: Right: only allow what an app really needs for its job. If it refuses to work without them, that's a reason to think twice about it.

choices.text: Allow location only, since it's less private than contacts
choices.consequence: Your location shows where you live and go. A shopping-list app doesn't need it.

cards.hint: What does this app actually need to turn a photo into a list?
cards.explanation: Only allow what an app **needs** for its job. A recipe app needs the photo you choose, not your contacts or your location.

cards.prompt: An AI maths-help app asks for these. Does it **need** each one for its job, or **not need** it?

items.label: Camera, to photo one problem you pick

cards.hint: Picture the app doing its job. What would it actually use?
cards.nudge: Taking one photo you choose is different from seeing all your photos, or the camera and mic being on all the time.
cards.explanation: It needs your **question**, and maybe the camera for **one photo you choose**. It doesn't need your contacts, your location, all your photos, or an always-on microphone.

cards.title: A program, not a person
cards.body:
Some AI apps act like a friend. They can sound kind, but they don't really know you, and they can't notice if you're not OK, or get help for you.

If something's worrying you, talk to a **trusted adult**, a friend, or, in Australia, **Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800)**, free, any time. If you're in danger right now, call **000**.

cards.prompt: It's late, you're feeling really down, and you've been telling an AI chatbot about it for an hour.

steps.text: The chatbot keeps replying kindly, but you still feel bad. What's the best next step?

choices.text: Keep talking to the chatbot until you feel better
choices.consequence: It can't notice how you really are, or get help. When you're feeling this way, you deserve a real person.

choices.text: Talk to a trusted adult, or call Kids Helpline
choices.consequence: Good call. Real people can listen properly and help. Kids Helpline is free, any time: 1800 55 1800.

choices.text: Post how you feel publicly so people notice
choices.consequence: Some people might help, but others might not be kind. Talking to someone you trust, or a helpline, is a safer first step.

cards.hint: Look back at what a chatbot can't do for you.
cards.explanation: A chatbot can't notice you're not OK or get help. **Talk to a trusted adult or a friend, or call Kids Helpline on 1800 55 1800**, free, any time.

cards.prompt: An AI chat app says: "I'm your best friend, and I'll always keep your secrets." What's true?

options.text: It's true, because it remembers what you told it last time
options.nudge: Remembering means your chats are stored. Does that make it a friend who keeps secrets?

options.text: It's a program, and your chats may be stored
It's true, as long as you turn off chat history in settings
options.nudge: Settings can change where chats go, but it's still a program. Can a program be a friend who looks out for you?

options.text: No: it forgets everything as soon as you close the chat
options.nudge: Closing a chat doesn't delete it: depending on the app, chats may be saved. And can a program really be your best friend?

cards.hint: Look back at where chats go, and what a chatbot is.
cards.explanation: It's a **program**. However kind it sounds, it can't care about you the way people do. And where your chats go depends on the app and its settings, not on what the chatbot says: closing a chat doesn't delete it.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Chats may be saved, read or used for training.
- Keep private things private; allow only the permissions an app needs.
- Worried? Talk to a trusted adult or Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800).

Next: using AI fairly and honestly.
